brief:
Palestinian journalists say they face pressure to depoliticize coverage of their own lives and experiences, according to Mondoweiss. The article argues that Palestinian reporters naming their grief and documenting their communities' realities encounter accusations of bias simply for reporting from their own perspective. Writers contend that neutrality in journalism is often demanded selectively of those reporting on their own societies.

The piece examines how Palestinian identity itself becomes labeled "ideological" when journalists report on matters directly affecting their communities and families. Contributors emphasize they did not choose to make their identity political, yet find that straightforward documentation of Palestinian experiences gets dismissed as activism rather than journalism. The article suggests this dynamic creates a double standard in how newsroom objectivity is assessed across different reporters and backgrounds.
dek: I didn't choose to make my identity political. But for Palestinian journalists, even naming our own grief and experiences gets branded as 'ideological'.
title: Palestinian journalists resist framing of identity as ideology
